translation_notes: Environment: neither kgraphpy nor linkml_runtime is installed in the study venv. context_shim.py imports the REAL kgraphpy (CIMGraph, CIMProcessor, Provenance, unmodified) from the pinned clone corpus/repos/statnett__KGraphPy (same commit 38859be), and, only when linkml_runtime is absent, registers empty stand-ins for the four names kgraphpy imports from it (SchemaView, SchemaDefinition, SlotDefinition, TypeDefinition), which this region never calls. original.py and translated.ldpy gain one identical line `import context_shim`.

`otherg.add((URIRef("s1"), URIRef("p1"), Literal("o")))` becomes `@graph otherg` + `+{ <s1> <p1> "o" }`; the draft's `otherg += g{ ... }` was replaced because it builds a throw-away graph (a different code path: CIMGraph.__iadd__ instead of add). The membership assert on `pr.graph` becomes `assert m{ <s1> <p1> "o" }(pr.graph)`, the receiver being an attribute, hence the call suffix. The identifiers URIRef("self_graph") / URIRef("other_graph") become <self_graph> / <other_graph> (no @base in scope, so identical relative IRIs); `g += otherg` is a whole-graph union, no island involved.

The region is a test returning None, printing nothing and mutating nothing visible, so a driver that only calls it shows nothing. The driver calls it four times, patching kgraphpy.graph.CIMGraph.__iadd__ in the call callable (restored by the next call): unpatched (all asserts pass), merges nothing, merges without provenance entry, merges a different object. The original raises AssertionError at a different assert each time; a raise is compared like a value. Verified by breaking the translation twice: another literal in +{ } fails call 1, a widened `?x` in the final m{ } fails call 4 (call 4 exists precisely for that).
Finding (minor): the AssertionError messages are empty, so two failures at different asserts cannot be told apart by the harness; discrimination rests on which call raises.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the triple written twice (the add, then the membership assert) becomes one `triple` local; nothing else to compress: the rest is the test's asserts, kept one per line so that a failure still points at its line.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the add becomes `+{ <s1> <p1> "o" }(otherg)` (call suffix: one statement where the translation designated otherg with @graph for a single write), the membership assert `assert m{ <s1> <p1> "o" }(pr.graph)`, the two identifiers relative IRIs (no @base in scope). `g += otherg` is a graph union and stays Python.

Exception to the symmetry: optimized.ldpy has no `triple` local, because the island writes the three terms in fewer tokens than a Python variable would cost, and an island cannot take a tuple anyway; the local exists only on the Python side, where it is the compression.
header_optimization_notes: Python: Namespace goes; URIRef, Literal, the kgraphpy imports and `import context_shim` stay.
LD Python: the whole rdflib import goes (the terms are written in the islands); the kgraphpy imports and `import context_shim` stay.
